summary: Add GET /api/alerts/trends?days=N returning one zero-filled bucket per UTC calendar day (oldest-first) for the last N days (default 7, min 1, max 90), each with a total count and a per-severity count, reusing the Severity enum ordering already used by the summary endpoint.
exact_source_files: AlertService.DTO/Responses/AlertTrendsResponse.cs + AlertTrendBucketResponse.cs (new; bucket = Date, TotalCount, SeverityCounts: AlertSeverityCountsResponse)
AlertService.Data.SQL/Repositories/AlertRepository.cs (implement GetTrendsAsync: group by CreatedDate.Date + Severity within [fromDateUtc, toDateUtc])
AlertService.API/Services/AlertManagementService.cs (implement: compute day window via TimeProvider, zero-fill all days/severities, oldest-first)
exact_source_files_note: Exceeds the default 5-file cap deliberately: a new read endpoint requires a query DTO, two new response DTOs, a repository contract + EF Core implementation, a service contract + implementation, and a controller action, touching every layer per repo-profile.md layering (Common -> DTO -> Data -> Data.SQL -> API service/controller). This is the smallest file set that satisfies all acceptance criteria.
adjacent_dependencies: AlertService.Models/Alert.cs, AlertDbContext, EF migrations: None (read-only query over existing CreatedDate/Severity columns, no schema change)
constraints: Days query param: default 7, minimum 1, maximum 90; invalid (out-of-range or non-numeric) must yield 400 with ValidationProblemDetails, consistent with the existing [ApiController] automatic model-state-to-ValidationProblemDetails behavior already relied on by AlertQueryRequest.Page/PageSize
Buckets are one per UTC calendar day for the last N days, oldest-first, including days/severities with zero alerts

Severity ordering within each bucket's per-severity breakdown must match the existing summary endpoint convention: Low, Medium, High, Critical (AlertSeverityCountsResponse property order / Severity enum order)
Day/severity counts must reflect alert CREATION date (CreatedDate), not IsActive state; do not filter by IsActive
Use the existing injected TimeProvider (not DateTime.UtcNow) in AlertManagementService to compute 'today' for testability, consistent with AlertManagementService's existing TimeProvider usage
coverage_goals: New GetTrendsAsync service logic: default days, explicit days, zero-count day/severity fill, oldest-first ordering
New repository GetTrendsAsync: day-boundary grouping, severity grouping, empty-range result
New controller action: 200 OK happy path, 400 ValidationProblemDetails for days=0, days=91, and non-numeric days

design_decisions.day_window_anchor: AlertManagementService.GetTrendsAsync computes today = _timeProvider.GetUtcNow().UtcDateTime.Date (same TimeProvider field already injected for CreatedDate/suppression logic); fromDateUtc = today.AddDays(-(request.Days - 1)); toDateUtc = today. Window is inclusive of today and the prior (Days - 1) days, totalling Days buckets.
design_decisions.aggregation_split: Repository GetTrendsAsync returns only non-zero (Date, Severity, Count) rows grouped via EF Core GroupBy over [fromDateUtc, toDateUtc] (mirrors GetSummaryAsync's GroupBy/Select aggregation shape); the service layer owns zero-filling every day in the requested range and every Severity value (Low/Medium/High/Critical) so the repository stays a thin aggregation query and all zero-count business rules live in one place, consistent with how GetSummaryAsync splits raw counts (repository) from DTO shaping (service).
design_decisions.route_shape: New sibling action GET api/alerts/trends (alongside the existing GET api/alerts/summary), bound via [FromQuery] AlertTrendsQueryRequest so DataAnnotations [Range] validation triggers the same automatic 400 ValidationProblemDetails path already exercised by AlertQueryRequest.Page/PageSize; no custom ApiBehaviorOptions needed since none exists today.
design_decisions.response_shape: AlertTrendsResponse { IReadOnlyList<AlertTrendBucketResponse> Buckets }; AlertTrendBucketResponse { DateOnly Date (or DateTime at UTC midnight, matching repo's existing DateTime-only usage since no DateOnly precedent exists), int TotalCount, AlertSeverityCountsResponse SeverityCounts } reusing the existing AlertSeverityCountsResponse (Low/Medium/High/Critical) from the summary endpoint instead of inventing a new severity-count shape.

out_of_scope: Changes to GET /api/alerts/summary (unchanged; only reused as the severity-ordering/shape convention)
Any change to Alert CRUD endpoints or entity schema
Timezone/locale handling beyond UTC calendar days
Caching or pre-aggregation of trend data
